title: Homily XI
subtitle: Matthew 3:7
author: chrysostom
excerpt: “But when he saw many of the Pharisees and Sadducees come to his baptism, he said unto them, O generation of vipers, who hath warned you to flee from the wrath…

footnotes.13: The correct reading seems to be ὅτε, “when,” not ὅτι, “that.”—R]
footnotes.17: Matt. iii. 10. [R.V., “And even now is the axe laid,” etc.—R.]
footnotes.21: See Amos v. 18; Jer. xvii. 15; Ezek. xii. 22, 27.
footnotes.28: Matt. iii. 11. Comp. Luke iii. 16. [In neither passage is the preposition repeated in the Greek text. Chrysostom (see sec. 6) interprets “fire” as part of the blessing promised. So many modern commentators.—R.]
footnotes.32: John i. 29; Engl. Vers. in marg. [So R.V. marg. The Greek phrase is ὁ αρων, “he that taketh up.”—R.]
footnotes.33: [ατν ναλαβεν is the better supported reading, but various conjectural emendations occur. “Himself to assume it,” is the most literal rendering.—R.]
footnotes.35: John i. 33, 34. [ R.V. more correctly, “I have seen, and have borne witness,” etc. The Greek perfects are to be taken in their grammatical sense, as the comment of Chrysostom implies.—R.]
footnotes.44: [The better supported text seems to be ατς, without ὁ χριστς; the latter is an explanatory gloss.—R.]
footnotes.45: “The Mystery:” i.e., Christ’s Baptism by Fire, His dwelling in our hearts by His Spirit. Comp. Col. i. 26, 27; Eph. i. 9, 10; iii. 9.
footnotes.47: [“The loosing of death, the abolition of sins,” etc., “the entrance into Paradise,” etc. The construction is the same throughout the list.—R.]
footnotes.51: [The first clause stands independently in the Greek text, forming the conclusion of the preceding paragraph. The new exhortation begins, “But I beseech again,” etc.—R.]
